d: To provide expert diagnostic imaging and clinical leadership at the Diagnostics & Imaging Center, and to oversee the safe, efficient and high-quality delivery of all unit activities. The Consultant Radiologist supervises staff, ensures compliance with clinical, safety, regulatory, accreditation and research standards, and contributes to the excellence of radiology practice through research, audit, education and training.
q: MBBS or equivalent medical degree from a recognized university.

Specialist qualification in Diagnostic Radiology from a recognized university or board (e.g., Fellowship, American Board, Canadian Board, FRCR, Arab Board, Kuwait Board, or a Ph.D. or equivalent), recognized by the Kuwait Ministry of Health.
Sub-specialty fellowship training (e.g., body, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular imaging or MRI) is desirable.
Valid license to practice as a Consultant Radiologist in the State of Kuwait, or eligibility to obtain it before starting.
Basic Life Support (BLS) and Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) from the American Heart Association, kept current.
ICH Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certificate, or completion within three months of appointment and renewal as required.
Radiation protection training, as required by national regulations.
Demonstrated experience in an administrative, leadership, or supervisory role in a radiology department.
Experience in radiography, ultrasound and color Doppler imaging, multislice CT, MRI and bone densitometry (DXA).
Experience in clinical research or clinical trial imaging is desirable.
r: Act as the subject-matter expert for diagnostic imaging and provide general clinical duties of a Consultant Radiologist.

Perform, interpret and report on radiological examinations and procedures, including MRI, CT, ultrasound (including Doppler), bone mineral densitometry (DXA), and general radiography, and image-guided procedures within the scope of competence.

Review imaging requests for clinical justification and appropriateness (using evidence-based appropriateness criteria); approve, modify or decline requests and select the most appropriate examination and protocol.
Establish, approve and periodically review imaging protocols for all modalities, including contrast and research-specific protocols.
Supervise, verify and approve radiology reports issued by the Diagnostic Imaging Center, ensuring they are accurate, clear, structured where appropriate, and issued within agreed turnaround times.
Communicate critical and unexpected findings to the referring clinician promptly and document this in line with the critical results policy.
Provide continuous consultative support to referring physicians and medical staff across DDI and participate in multidisciplinary meetings.
Apply knowledge of imaging relevant to diabetes and metabolic disease (e.g., body composition, hepatic fat quantification, vascular and diabetic-foot imaging) in clinical and research work.

Radiation safety: ensure justification and optimization of all ionizing radiation examinations; oversee dose monitoring against diagnostic reference levels; ensure pregnancy screening and compliance with Kuwait Ministry of Health radiation protection regulations, in coordination with the Radiation Protection Department.
MRI safety: oversee MRI safety zoning, patient and staff screening, and decisions on implants and devices, in line with recognized MR safety guidance.

Contrast safety: oversee contrast screening (renal function, allergy history, metformin and other diabetes-related risks), administration under appropriate supervision, and management of contrast reactions and extravasation.
Ensure availability of resuscitation equipment and drugs in the Diagnostic Imaging Center and lead the clinical response to medical emergencies in the unit.
Ensure informed consent is obtained and documented for procedures requiring it.
Report, investigate and follow up on incidents and near-misses, and ensure corrective and preventive actions are implemented.
Ensure compliance with infection prevention and control practices with the respective unit.
Provide clinical and operational oversight of all activities and ensure implementation of operational policies and procedures.
Supervise, direct and support staff, including radiologists, radiographers/technologists, sonographers, nurses and administrative staff.
Plan duty rosters, coverage and on-call arrangements to meet service demand and supervise on-call duties as required.
Conduct or contribute to staff performance appraisals, competency assessments and privileging of radiology staff.
Participate in interview panels to ensure selection of the best possible candidates for appointments in the department.
Monitor workload, waiting times, scheduling efficiency and utilization of equipment, and take action to address bottlenecks.
Oversee equipment performance, preventive maintenance, quality control and vendor service contracts, and ensure timely escalation of faults.
Oversee the safe and effective use of RIS/PACS, image storage, retrieval, and data integrity.
Contribute to strategic and operational planning for the department, including manpower, equipment, facilities, the annual budget estimate and running costs.
Organize and chair professional meetings within the department and coordinate with other units (including Clinical Operations) to improve patient care, in consultation with the Head of Unit.
Deputize for the Head of Unit when delegated and assist with administrative work.
Lead the Diagnostic Imaging Center quality assurance and improvement program, including clinical audits, radiologist peer reviews, and discrepancy meetings.
Define, monitor, and report on key performance indicators to the Head of Unit and relevant committees.

Ensure policies, procedures and practices meet internationally recognized accreditation standards adopted by DDI (e.g., Accreditation Canada International), and support accreditation surveys and audits.
Ensure compliance with documented clinical standards, policies and procedures to maintain a consistently high standard of care.
Keep policies and procedures current and aligned with best practice and regulatory requirements.
Promote, encourage and participate in research activities, including acting as principal investigator, co-investigator or study radiologist as required.
Review study protocols and imaging manuals for feasibility, and advise on imaging methodology, acquisition parameters, standardization and quantitative endpoints.

Ensure research imaging is performed and reported according to the approved protocol, ICH Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ethics committee approvals and sponsor requirements, including blinded or independent reads where specified.
Ensure research participants have given valid informed consent before research imaging is performed, and that research and clinical imaging are clearly separated in scheduling, reporting and billing.
Oversee the management and communication of incidental findings in research participants according to the approved protocol and DDI policy.
Oversee scanner qualification, phantom testing and calibration required for research studies, and ensure de-identification, secure transfer and archiving of research images and data.
Maintain study documentation (delegation logs, training records, source documents), respond to data queries, and support monitoring visits, audits and regulatory inspections.
Contribute to scientific publications and presentations arising from the unit’s research.
Organize and participate in continuing professional and medical education for unit staff.
Teach and train radiology staff, residents, students and other healthcare professionals, and support the professional development of unit staff.
Maintain personal continuing medical education and professional development in line with licensing requirements.

Respect and maintain the privacy and dignity of patients and research participants, and keep all clinical, research and institutional information confidential always, in line with DDI policies and applicable regulations.
Uphold professional and ethical standards and declare any conflicts of interest.
Perform any other related duties assigned by the Head of Unit.

The Consultant Radiologist has direct clinical and operational supervisory responsibility for all unit staff, including radiologists/specialists, radiographers/technologists, sonographers, nurses, research imaging staff and administrative/reception staff. This includes allocation of work, supervision of clinical practice, approval of radiology reports, performance evaluation, competency assessment, and enforcement of unit policies and procedures.

d: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

We are looking for an outstanding storytelling and narrative development lead to lead our content marketing team. Canonical has a robust portfolio of open source products and offers support for a wide range of open source technologies. This role is for someone who cares deeply about narrative quality and wants to elevate our brand positioning. It requires process discipline and creative smarts, leadership skills and performance-driven strategy to ensure our content aligns with our business objectives.

The ideal candidate is passionate about technology, technology marketing and the use of technology in marketing. They would love to gain experience optimizing content processes, coaching others on their narrative skills and building brand authority. They enjoy learning and improving themselves, the team and the organization. They problem solve, get hands-on, experiment, measure and use automation to make daily life easier. To succeed in this role, the candidate must be metrics-driven, highly organized and skilled at team development, capacity planning and cross-functional collaboration.
This role reports to the Director of Communications.
Location: This role is home based in the EMEA region.
What your day will look like
Develop and execute a content strategy that aligns with our business goals, SEO and brand.
Manage our content calendar end to end, ensuring content is efficiently produced with minimum friction and process clarity.
Ensure content quality, consistency and brand alignment in everything we produce.
Collaborate with our web and growth engineering teams to optimize content for search and AI engines, building on proven SEO or GEO expertise.
Supervise quarterly content planning sessions and work closely with content specialists, product management and marketing to optimize content plans.
Monitor and report on KPIs for our content program and use analytics tools to identify improvement opportunities.
Align messaging to ensure integrated campaign support across channels, working closely with our marketing, product and brand teams.
What we are looking for in you
At least 5 years of work experience in content or related roles, preferably at technology companies, with 2+ years of experience as a manager or team lead.
Proven experience creating authoritative and engaging content. Portfolio of written work required.
Applied knowledge of GEO and SEO, experience with relevant tools and SEO-driven content calendars.
Excellent project management and interpersonal skills with the ability to create highly efficient processes for content production and reuse.
Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications or a relevant discipline.
Someone who is passionate about technology and open source.
A problem solver: you don’t shy away from taking on challenges and see projects through to completion.
Attention to detail and appreciation for standards: you value quality and accuracy but can adapt quickly when the need arises.
